---
title: Tools with input
description: A form is a tool with an inputSchema. The cursor types the agent's values into your form's fields, your form library hears it, and fill shows what it cannot type.
sidebar:
  label: 2. Tools with input
---

A form is not a special kind of tool. It is **a tool with an `inputSchema`**: the agent sends values, the cursor types
each one into the field it belongs to, and your form library hears the typing like a person's. `execute` is the
function the form already submits to. There is no `form` option, no adapter and no second hook.

## A complete example

shadcn/ui's `Form` on React Hook Form, with one zod schema for the agent's call and the person's submit. To follow
along, add the components this page uses (`form` brings React Hook Form, its zod resolver and zod with it):

```package-install
npx shadcn@latest add form input select label
```

An agent calls `add_to_cart({ size: "L", quantity: 2 })`:

1. **The schema checks the input.** Input that fails it never reaches the page: the agent gets the schema's messages
   back, and the cursor does not move.
2. **The cursor types what it can.** It goes to the button named "Add to cart" (the tool's `title`), then types 2 into
   the field named `quantity`. React Hook Form's `onChange` hears it.
3. **`fill` puts the rest on screen.** The Size is a shadcn `Select`, a custom widget with nothing to type into, so
   `form.reset(values)` shows L.
4. **The cursor presses the button, and `add` runs.** Its return value is the agent's answer.

A person's submit goes through `form.handleSubmit`, which validates and calls `add`. An agent's call reaches `add`
directly, after the tool's own schema: the action is written once and runs once.

## How the cursor fills a form

The cursor finds a parameter's field by the field's `name`, then by a label that matches the schema's `title` for it
or the parameter read as words (`firstName` is "first name"). It looks outward from the tool's button, so the closest
field wins. Then it writes the value the way the control expects:

| Control | What happens |
|---|---|
| Text, email, tel, search, textarea | Typed a character at a time |
| `number`, `date`, `range`, a native `<select>` | Written once |
| Checkbox, radio | Clicked to match the value (in a radio group, the one whose `value` is the parameter's) |
| A custom widget: shadcn `Select`, `Combobox`, a date picker | Visited and highlighted, never written: use `fill` |

`fill` runs after the cursor typed what it could and before it presses or parks. It may return a promise, which is
awaited. With the cursor off, with reduced motion, or after the person moved the mouse, the values the cursor did not
type are written in one step, and `fill` still runs.

A number input hands React Hook Form a string, and a `z.number()` schema rejects it: pass
`e.target.valueAsNumber` to `field.onChange`, as the example does.

## When the fields are not named like the parameters

A parameter with no field is skipped: nothing is typed, and `execute` still gets the value. When the field has another
name, say where it is with `fields`, by parameter:

```tsx
useWebTool({
  id: "search_flights",
  description: "Search one-way flights between two airports.",
  inputSchema: searchSchema,
  fields: {
    from: "Leaving from", // the field labelled "Leaving from"
    to: { role: "combobox", name: "Going to" }, // a locator
    cabin: false, // never type this one
  },
  execute: search,
});
```

A field elsewhere on the page is typed there. A tool with no control at all types nothing unless `fields` names a
field.

## Validation errors are the answer

Two layers, and both reach the agent as readable text with an [error code](/concepts/errors):

- **The schema.** Input that fails it is `invalid_input`, with each bad field named, before anything is typed. The
  agent fixes its call and retries.
- **Your own rules**, inside the action: throw a `WebToolError` with a code, and put the same words on the page, so the
  person sees what the agent read.

```tsx
const add = ({ size, quantity }: AddToCartInput) => {
  if (!inStock(size, quantity)) {
    const message = `Only ${stockOf(size)} left in size ${size}.`;
    form.setError("root", { message });
    throw new WebToolError("invalid_input", message);
  }
  // …
};
```

Show `form.formState.errors.root?.message` under the form. A person's submit runs the same function, so a throw there
is a rejected `handleSubmit`; catch it in the submit handler if you would rather not see it in the console. A tool that
has to ask the person something ("which size?") calls [`waitingForUser`](/reference/core/waiting-for-user) and answers
with `needs_user`.

:::note[A form that leaves its page]
Navigate inside the action, with your router's own `navigate`, after the work is done. `useWebTool` keeps the tool
registered until the agent has its answer, so nothing else is needed.
:::

## TanStack Form

The same hook works with any form library: the cursor writes a field the way a person does (the native setter, then
`input` and `change` events), so any controlled input hears it. Here it is with TanStack Form:

```package-install
npm install @tanstack/react-form
```

Give each input the field's name (`name={field.name}`): TanStack Form does not set it, and it is how the cursor finds
the field. For a custom widget, `fill` calls `form.setFieldValue(…)`. Skyline's traveler form
(`apps/flights/src/tools/TravelerDetailsForm.tsx`) is a larger one, with a field per traveler.

## Try it

Render `<AddToCart />` on a page, then in the browser console:

```js
await agent.invoke("add_to_cart", { size: "L", quantity: 2 });
```

The cursor types 2 into Quantity, the Size shows L, the cursor presses **Add to cart**, and the call answers "Added 2 ×
Ocean Tee, size L." Try `quantity: 0`: the cursor stays put, and the call rejects with `invalid_input`, naming the bad
field.

## Options you'll use most

| Option | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `inputSchema` | The parameters, as a zod (or any Standard Schema) object or JSON Schema. Validated before anything moves. |
| `fill` | Put values on screen yourself, for widgets the cursor cannot type into. |
| `fields` | Where each parameter is typed, when the field is not named like it: a label, a locator, or `false`. |
| `target` | Which button the cursor presses, when the `title` does not name it. |
| `execute` | The action, shared with the form's submit. Its return value is the answer. |

Every option: [`useWebTool`](/reference/react/use-web-tool) and [`defineWebTool`](/reference/core/define-web-tool).
